title: AC Not Cooling? 9 Causes and What Each Fix Costs in Chennai
excerpt: Nine reasons your AC blows warm air, arranged from the free two-minute fix to the ₹15,000 repair. Honest Chennai costs for each, plus what you can safely do yourself.

sections.heading: Start cheap, work up
paragraphs: When an AC stops cooling in a Chennai May, the instinct is to fear the worst — a dead compressor, a ₹15,000 bill. In practice, most no-cooling complaints trace back to something far cheaper, and two of the nine causes below cost nothing to fix. Work through them in order, from free to costly, and you will either solve it yourself or know exactly what a fair quote looks like.

sections.heading: Causes 1 and 2: wrong settings and a choked filter (free)
paragraphs: Before assuming the worst, check the remote. A surprising share of no-cooling calls in Chennai end with a mode change. Make sure the AC is on Cool mode — the snowflake icon — not Dry or Fan. Set the temperature to 24°C or lower and the fan speed to high. Check for an active sleep timer or eco mode quietly raising the set point overnight. Cost of this fix: zero.

Next, the filter. Chennai's dust load means filters choke within four to six weeks in summer. A blocked filter starves the indoor coil of airflow, so the AC runs but the room barely cools. Pop open the front panel, slide the mesh filters out, rinse them under a tap, dry, and refit. Ten minutes, zero rupees, and it fixes more cooling complaints than any other single step.
bullets: Cool mode on, temperature at 24°C or below, fan speed high
Sleep timer and eco mode switched off
Filters rinsed, dried, and refitted every four to six weeks in summer
Doors and windows actually shut while you test

sections.heading: Causes 3 and 4: dirty coils and a starved outdoor unit
paragraphs: If the filter is clean and airflow still feels weak, the evaporator coil behind it is likely coated in grime — cause three. Chennai's mix of dust, humidity, and, near the coast, salt-laden air builds a film on the coil fins that blocks heat transfer. The AC blows air, just not cold air. A basic service starts from ₹499; a deep or jet clean, which flushes the coil and drain tray properly, starts from ₹799.

The outdoor condenser works even harder — cause four is simply a starved one. Parked on a balcony at 40°C, boxed in by cartons, drying laundry, or overgrown plants, it cannot dump heat into already-hot air. Add a dust-caked or salt-corroded coil and cooling drops sharply while power bills climb. Keep 30 cm of clear space on every side, and get both units jet cleaned; the deep clean from ₹799 covers coil and drain.

sections.heading: Causes 5 and 6: voltage swings and a failed capacitor
paragraphs: Chennai's summer grid sags exactly when every AC in the street switches on. Low or fluctuating voltage can stop the compressor from starting — the indoor fan blows, but the outdoor unit stays silent or clicks on and off. If your lights dim when the AC kicks in, suspect voltage. A good stabilizer costs ₹1,500 to ₹3,500 depending on tonnage; inverter ACs tolerate wider swings but are not immune, especially on older wiring.

The run capacitor is the most common electrical casualty of heat and voltage swings. When it weakens, the compressor hums, trips, or refuses to start, and the AC blows plain air. It is a small, inexpensive part but sits across live terminals that hold charge even after the power is off — not a DIY job. Expect ₹600 to ₹1,500 fitted, depending on the rating, and most technicians can swap it in a single visit.

sections.heading: Cause 7: the gas leak — most misdiagnosed, most overbilled
paragraphs: Refrigerant does not get used up. If your AC needs gas, it has a leak — usually at a flare joint, a corroded coil, or pipework nicked during installation. Coastal humidity accelerates copper corrosion, so leaks are more common in Chennai than owners expect. A top-up without finding the leak buys you a few weeks, then the same complaint returns with the same bill.

Honest pricing looks like this: a gas top-up starts from ₹1,499, and a full R32 gas charge runs ₹2,500 to ₹3,500. Insist on leak detection and repair before recharging — a nitrogen pressure test or soap-solution check at every joint. If a technician quotes a recharge without once mentioning where the gas went, get a second opinion.
bullets: Ice forming on the copper pipes or indoor coil
Hissing or bubbling sounds near the indoor unit
Air from the vents is cool, never cold
Oily residue around pipe joints or valves
Cooling that faded over weeks, not overnight

sections.heading: Causes 8 and 9: PCB and compressor, the big-ticket repairs
paragraphs: The PCB is the AC's brain, and Chennai's voltage spikes are its most common killer. Symptoms: blinking error lights, a unit that ignores the remote, or an outdoor unit that never gets the start signal. Repair or replacement runs ₹1,499 to ₹4,999 depending on board and brand — inverter boards sit at the top of that range. Always ask whether the board can be repaired at component level before paying for a full replacement.

The compressor is the costliest failure. Warning signs: loud starts, repeated tripping of your MCB, or an outdoor unit that hums but moves no refrigerant. Compressor work starts from ₹4,999, and a full replacement with gas can reach ₹8,000 to ₹15,000 depending on tonnage and brand. On an AC older than eight to ten years, weigh that quote against a new unit — sometimes replacement is the smarter spend.

sections.heading: The cost ladder: DIY or call?
paragraphs: The line is simple: settings, filters, and clearing space around the outdoor unit are yours. Everything involving refrigerant, capacitors, boards, or the sealed system needs a trained technician — the gas is under pressure and the capacitor holds a charge even when the power is off. A wrong DIY move on either turns a ₹1,500 problem into a ₹5,000 one.

bullets: DIY, free: remote settings, filter wash, clearing the outdoor unit
₹499-₹799: basic service or deep coil cleaning
₹1,499-₹3,500: gas top-up to full R32 charge, after leak repair

takeaways: Check remote settings and wash the filter before booking anything — it is free and solves many cases
Dirty coils are Chennai's most common paid fix; deep cleaning starts from ₹799
Never pay for a gas top-up without leak detection — refrigerant does not run out on its own
Capacitor and PCB faults usually trace back to voltage swings; a stabilizer is cheap insurance
On ACs past eight to ten years, compare compressor repair quotes against buying a new unit

faqs.question: How much does it cost to fix an AC that is not cooling in Chennai?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the cause. A cleaning-related fix runs ₹499 to ₹799, a capacitor swap ₹600 to ₹1,500, gas work ₹1,499 to ₹3,500, and PCB or compressor repairs range from ₹1,499 to well past ₹4,999. A proper diagnosis first saves you from paying for the wrong fix.

faqs.question: Why does my AC need a gas top-up every summer?
faqs.answer: Because it has an unrepaired leak. Refrigerant circulates in a sealed loop and never gets consumed, so a yearly top-up means gas is escaping — often through a corroded joint, which Chennai's coastal humidity accelerates. Ask for leak detection and repair before the next recharge.

faqs.question: Is it worth repairing the compressor, or should I replace the AC?
faqs.answer: If the unit is under eight years old and the compressor may still be covered by the manufacturer's warranty, repair usually makes sense. For older machines, compressor work from ₹4,999 — often ₹8,000 to ₹15,000 all-in — approaches the price of a new, more efficient AC. Compare both quotes before deciding.
